Calderon, Oakland, CA, for the latter to continue to provide 5 days a week of after school programming in Visual Arts, in an additional amount of $26,500.00, increasing the not to exceed amount of the Contract from $26,500.00 to $53,000.00 and extending the Contract term from August 12, 2019 through December 31, 2019 to May 28, 2020 at Elmhurst United Middle School. All other terms and conditions of the Contract remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $26,500 and extends an after school visual arts contract at Elmhurst United Middle to $53,000
summary: This amends a contract so an independent contractor can keep running after school visual arts classes five days a week at Elmhurst United Middle School. The limit doubles from $26,500 to $53,000 and the end date moves from December 31, 2019 to May 28, 2020.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Contract - School Specialty Children's Publishing - Special Education Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Contract between the District and School Specialty Children's Publishing, Greenville, WI, for the latter to provide two trainings on the buy-back day, one training will be to ensure any new teachers or teachers who missed the trainings in the fall, and the other training will hone in on deficits identified by teachers through feedback from teachers and observations; provide two days of trainings where they will go to multiple school sites to observe and provide feedback to improving training; facilitate training to select teacher and central office leaders to become "trainers of trainers" in order to further support the district; and loop back and consult with individual teachers that require reteaching, or guided individual support, for the period of October 1, 2019 through August 31, 2020, in the additional amount of $68,000.00, increasing the Contract not to exceed amount from $132,000.00 to $200,000.00, via the Special Education Department.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $68,000 to School Specialty Children's Publishing's special education teacher training, to $200,000
summary: This amends a contract for teacher trainings run through the Special Education Department. They include two trainings on the buy-back day, school site visits with feedback, training for teachers and central office leaders to become trainers, and one-on-one support. The limit rises from $132,000 to $200,000 for October 2019 through August 2020.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding - United Parcel Service - Northern CA District - Adult and Career Education
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding between the District, on behalf of its Adult and Career Education Department, and United Parcel Service Northern California District, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide space at 8400 Pardee Drive, Oakland, CA 94621, where it is owner/leaseholder of real property, for the District to conduct adult education classes and programming services, for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022, at no cost to the District. .
headline: Approves a no-cost agreement for UPS to host adult education classes at its Pardee Drive site
summary: United Parcel Service Northern California District will provide space at 8400 Pardee Drive in Oakland for the district's Adult and Career Education Department to hold adult education classes. This memorandum of understanding (MOU) costs the district nothing and runs July 2019 through June 2022.
vendor_name: United Parcel Service Northern California District
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Grant Award - The California Wellness Foundation - OAL - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text:
Acceptance by the Board of Education of a Grant Award from the California Wellness Foundation, San Francisco, CA, as specified below:
·	$5,000.00 "For core operating support of Skyline High School's girls varsity basketball team to promote physical activity";
·	$5,000.00 "For core operating support of Oakland Technical High School's girls varsity basketball team to promote health through physical activity"; and
·	 $5,000.00 "For core operating support of Oakland High School's girls varsity basketball team for health and well-being through physical activity", 
for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, pursuant to the terms and conditions thereof, if any.
headline: Accepts three $5,000 California Wellness Foundation grants for girls varsity basketball
summary: The California Wellness Foundation gives $5,000 each to the girls varsity basketball teams at Skyline High School, Oakland Technical High School and Oakland High School, to support physical activity and health. The text lists three separate amounts and no total.
schools: Skyline High School; Oakland Technical High School; Oakland High School
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No.1, Grant Award - California Department of Education - CSPP 9020 - California State Preschool Program - Early Childhood Education Department
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1920-0178 - Approving Amendment No. 1, Contract No. CSPP-9020, California State Preschool Program between District and the California Department of Education, accepting grant award increase for the California State Preschool Program, operated by the Early Childhood Education Department, in the additional amount of $368,683.00, increasing the grant amount from $12,175,510.00 to $12,544,193.00, for the period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020, pursuant to term and conditions thereof, if any.
headline: Accepts $368,683 more from the state for the California State Preschool Program
summary: The board adopts a resolution accepting a grant increase from the California Department of Education for the State Preschool Program run by Early Childhood Education. The grant rises from $12,175,510 to $12,544,193 for July 2019 through June 2020.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Grant Award- California Department of Education - CCTR-9010 - General Child Care and Development Program - Early Childhood Education Department
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No 1920-0179 - Approving Amendment No. 1, Contract No. CCTR-9010 between District and the California Department of Education, accepting grant award increase for the California State Child Development Programs operated by the Early Childhood Education Department, in the additional amount of $177,453.00, increasing the grant amount from $2,586,937.00 to $2,764,390.00, for the period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020, pursuant to terms and conditions thereof, if any.
headline: Accepts $177,453 more from the state for child development programs
summary: The board adopts a resolution accepting a grant increase from the California Department of Education for child development programs run by Early Childhood Education. The grant rises from $2,586,937 to $2,764,390 for July 2019 through June 2020.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: First Amendment, Grant of Easement – Fruitvale Station LLC and Education for Change – Lazear Charter Academy
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of First Amendment, Grant of Easement by and between District (Grantor), Fruitvale Station, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (Grantee), and Education for Change (School Operator), pertaining to an easement located on 824 29th Avenue, Oakland, CA, delineating the terms and conditions under which Grantee approves and agrees that School Operator, subject to the provisions of the Facilities Use Agreement or otherwise with the express written consent of Grantor, shall have the right to: (a) place two (2) modular portable buildings on the Easement Area; and, (b) change the surface elevation of the Easement Area by more than one (1) foot. All other terms and conditions of the Grant of Easement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Amends an easement so Education for Change can place modular buildings at Lazear Charter Academy
summary: This amends an easement on 824 29th Avenue between the district, Fruitvale Station, LLC and Education for Change. It sets terms for placing two modular portable buildings and for changing the ground level there by more than one foot. No dollar amount is stated.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Gabriela Diaz - Charter Schools Office
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Gabriela Diaz, San Leandro, CA, for the latter to provide support in responding to calls and emails from families using the ZenDesk System, via Charter Schools Office, for the period of August 5, 2019 through December 20, 2019, in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for a contractor to answer family calls and emails for the Charter Schools Office
summary: A contractor will respond to calls and emails from families through the ZenDesk help system for the Charter Schools Office. The contract period began before the board vote and ended December 20, 2019.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Partnership for Children and Youth - Student Assignment Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Partnership for Children and Youth, El Cerrito, CA, for the latter to provide: staff to help facilitate and support with initial ELPAC testing, resulting in District students having accurate information for placement and accurate resources, via Student Assignment Department, for the period of October 1, 2019 through November 30, 2019, in an amount not to exceed $9,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $9,000 for Partnership for Children and Youth to help with English language testing
summary: Partnership for Children and Youth will provide staff to help run initial testing of students' English skills (the English Language Proficiency Assessments for California, or ELPAC) for the Student Assignment Department. The results help place students correctly. The contract period began before the board vote and ended November 30, 2019.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Lacey Cherice Wilson - Continuous School Improvement Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Lacey Cherice Wilson, Alameda, CA, for the latter to provide: support to the Kaiser School community members to engage in circle conversations in which they will share out about their school community, perspectives and insights with each other; conduct, following the foregoing, information gathering sessions with the help of a questionnaire; share data from the questionnaire and used same to inform the Kaiser/Sankofa design planning process, via Continuous School Improvement Department, for the period of September 23, 2019 through December 31, 2019, in an amount not to exceed $2,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $2,000 for community listening sessions to guide Kaiser and Sankofa school planning
summary: A contractor will lead circle conversations with the Kaiser school community, gather input with a questionnaire, and share the results to inform the Kaiser/Sankofa design planning process. The contract period began before the board vote and ended December 31, 2019.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Milton Reynolds - Board of Education - Director Shanthi Gonzales, District 6
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Milton Reynolds, San Leandro, CA, for the latter under the direction of District 6 Director, Shanthi Gonzales, to help facilitate community engagement meetings with several District 6 school communities; provide thought partnership around the design of community engagement meetings; capture and ensure follow-up on constituent recommendations, for the period beginning November 12, 2019 and ending December 31, 2019, in an amount not to exceed $6,000.00.
headline: Pays a consultant up to $6,000 to help run District 6 community engagement meetings
summary: The district hires a San Leandro consultant to work under the direction of the District 6 board member. The consultant will help facilitate community engagement meetings with several District 6 school communities, help design those meetings, and make sure constituent recommendations are followed up on. The contract runs from November 12, 2019 to December 31, 2019, so it began before the board's approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment, Board Policy 3150 – Business and Noninstruction Operations – Results-Based Budgeting
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment, Board Policy 3150 - Business and Noninstructional Operations - Results-Based Budgeting, establishing that the first draft of the District’s Local Control Accountability Plan (LCAP) and the District’s Budget shall be presented to the Board of Education and the community at a Board Meeting no later than the second Regular Board Meeting in May annually.
headline: Requires the draft budget and LCAP to go to the Board by the second May meeting each year
summary: This changes Board Policy 3150 on budgeting. The first draft of the Local Control Accountability Plan (LCAP) and the district budget must be presented to the Board and the community at a Board meeting no later than the second Regular Board Meeting in May each year. The item has no cost.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
